{{short description|Canadian biostatistician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=October 2025}}
{{Use Canadian English|date=October 2025}}
'''Shu Jiang''', also known as '''Joy Jiang''', is a Canadian [[biostatistician]] and tenured associate professor in the Division of Public Health Sciences at the [[Washington University School of Medicine]] in [[St. Louis]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Shu (Joy) Jiang, PhD {{!}} Department of Surgery {{!}} Washington University in St. Louis |url=https://surgery.wustl.edu/people/shu-joy-jiang/ |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=surgery.wustl.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sara |date=2022-11-08 |title=Board grants faculty appointments, tenure |url=https://source.washu.edu/2022/11/board-grants-faculty-appointments-tenure/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=The Source |language=en-US}}</ref> She is also the co-founder of Prognosia Inc with [[Graham Colditz]], a technology company that develops [[AI]] models that assess digital [[mammograms]] to accurately predict the risk of [[breast cancer]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2025 |title=Public company buys startup using WashU's AI technology to assess breast cancer risk |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/stlouis/inno/stories/news/2025/09/04/prognosia-washu-research-sold-to-lunit.html |access-date=October 17, 2025 |website=St. Louis Business Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> Prognosia's first tool, Prognosia Breast, earned Breakthrough Device Designation from the [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)]] in June 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis-Thompson |first=Marissanne |date=August 11, 2025 |title=WashU AI breast cancer risk detection software scores major FDA designation |url=https://www.stlpr.org/health-science-environment/2025-08-11/washu-ai-breast-cancer-risk-detection-software-scores-major-fda-designation |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=STLPR |language=en}}</ref> and the company was acquired by Lunit in September 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strait |first=Julia Evangelou |date=October 13, 2025 |title=AI breast cancer startup acquired by Lunit |url=https://medicine.washu.edu/news/breast-cancer-startup-founded-by-washu-medicine-researchers-acquired-by-lunit/ |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=WashU Medicine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-08 |title=Lunit submits 510(k) to U.S. FDA for breast cancer risk prediction model |url=https://www.auntminnie.com/imaging-informatics/artificial-intelligence/news/15773580/lunit-submits-510k-to-us-fda-for-breast-cancer-risk-prediction-model |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=AuntMinnie |language=en-us}}</ref>

Jiang is known for her methodological contributions to breast cancer risk prediction using high-dimensional mammogram images.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shu (Joy) Jiang |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=W-CNTTIAAAAJ |access-date=2026-03-07 |website=scholar.google.com (user=W-CNTTIAAAAJ)}}</ref> In April 2023, ''[[The New York Times]]'' and ''[[CNN]]'' interviewed Jiang for a feature about breast density and cancer risk, in which she discussed recent findings on how changes in density over time may indicate elevated breast cancer risk.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 28, 2023 |title=Researchers Identify Possible New Risk for Breast Cancer (Published 2023) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/28/health/breast-cancer-density.html |access-date=October 15, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Howard |first=Jacqueline |date=May 2, 2023 |title=Breast density changes over time could be linked to breast cancer risk, study finds |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/05/02/health/breast-density-cancer-study |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> In December 2024, ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'' cited Jiang in an article about artificial intelligence and breast cancer screening. Discussing her team's work on longitudinal mammogram analysis, Jiang said: "Our new method is able to detect subtle changes over time in repeated mammogram images that are not visible to the eye."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Healthday |date=December 6, 2024 |title=AI Reads Multiple Mammograms To Help Predict Breast Cancer Risk |url=https://www.usnews.com/news/health-news/articles/2024-12-06/ai-reads-multiple-mammograms-to-help-predict-breast-cancer-risk |access-date=October 15, 2025 |work=U.S. News and World Report}}</ref> More recently, media coverage has also included BreastCancer.org, which described a newer AI-based approach in which Jiang used multiple years of mammograms to enhance risk prediction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Study: AI Tool Uses Multiple Years of Mammograms to Predict Risk |url=https://www.breastcancer.org/news/ai-tool-mammograms-predict-risk |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=www.breastcancer.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

She is an associate editor for the journal ''[[Biometrics (journal)|Biometrics]]''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Associate Editors |url=https://biometrics.biometricsociety.org/home/associate-editors |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=biometrics.biometricsociety.org |language=en-US}}</ref> and a statistical reviewer for ''[[JAMA Network Open]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=JAMA Network Open |title=JAMA Network Open Masthead |url=https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2839516 |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=JAMA Network}}</ref>  Among other awards and honors, Jiang has been named a ''[[Forbes]]'' 30 Under 30 in Healthcare in 2023<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Shu Jiang |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/shu-jiang/ |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Durando |first=Elizabethe Holland |date=December 21, 2022 |title=Shu Jiang named to Forbes 30 Under 30 list for health care |url=https://medicine.washu.edu/news/shu-jiang-named-to-forbes-30-under-30-list-for-health-care/ |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=WashU Medicine |language=en}}</ref> and received the [[National Institutes of Health MERIT Award|MERIT award]] from the [[National Cancer Institute]] (2021-2027).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=WashU Medicine Department of Surgery |year=2022 |title=2021 Annual Report. Out Mission in Action |url=https://surgery.wustl.edu/app/uploads/2024/02/DoS-Annual-Report-2021.pdf |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=wustl.edu}}</ref>

== Education ==
Jiang received a B.Sc. in statistics from [[Simon Fraser University]] (2012-2015), an M.Sc. in statistics from [[Western University (Canada)|Western University]] (2015-2016), and a Ph.D. in statistics from [[University of Waterloo]] (2016-2018), where her supervisor was Richard Cook.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Alumni: Joy Shu Jiang {{!}} Statistical Consulting and Survey Research Unit {{!}} University of Waterloo |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/statistical-consulting-survey-research-unit/news/our-alumni-joy-shu-jiang |access-date=2025-10-28 |website=uwaterloo.ca |language=en}}</ref> From 2018-2019, she trained as a postdoctoral fellow in biostatistics at the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]], where her supervisor was [[Rebecca Betensky]].<ref name=":3" />
